lesson.title: What could the offspring inherit?

steps.headline: Each parent passes on one allele of a gene, chosen at random.

lead.text: A gene can come in different versions called alleles. A diploid organism has two alleles of each gene, one from each parent. That pair is its genotype.
A genotype with two different alleles, such as Aa, is heterozygous. Each gamete gets one of the two alleles, at random.

steps.headline: A Punnett square lists every way two gametes can pair.

lead.text: Write one parent's gametes along the top and the other parent's down the side. Each box is one pairing, and every box is equally likely.
To find a chance, count the boxes of one genotype and divide by the total.

steps.headline: Cross Aa with Aa. How many of the four boxes are Aa?

workedSteps.text: Each parent's gametes are A or a. Fill the boxes.
Two of the boxes show Aa.
Divide by the total number of boxes.

steps.headline: Cross Aa with Aa. What percentage of offspring is expected to be aa?
A dominant allele shows even when only one copy is present.

lead.text: The phenotype is the trait you can see. With complete dominance, one copy of the dominant allele, A, is enough to show it.
The recessive trait appears only when both alleles are recessive, as in aa.
Cross a heterozygous parent with a parent that has two recessive alleles. Fill the four boxes, then ask which of them show the recessive trait.

reveal.text: You counted the aa boxes. Only genotype aa shows the recessive trait, and this cross fills half its boxes with it.

lead.text: A family has four children from an Aa × Aa cross. The chance of aa for each child comes straight from the square.

reveal.text: The square gives the chance for each child. It does not set how many of a family's children will have aa.

lesson.orientation: Use a single-gene cross while separating genotype, phenotype and probability.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: You flip two fair coins, one after the other.
Each coin lands heads or tails with equal chance.

intro.promise: By the end you'll use a Punnett square to predict the chances of each genotype and trait in a single-gene cross.
intro.whyItMatters: It is how breeders and genetic counsellors estimate the chances of a trait.

recap.keyIdea: Each parent passes on one allele at random, and a Punnett square counts the equally likely pairings. The chances apply to each child.

blocks.text: You found that two coins give 25% for two heads, and that Aa × Aa gives 25% for aa and 50% for Aa.
You also saw that a family of four need not follow the percentages.

recap.nextHook: Now ask where a new allele comes from in the first place. Where does a new variant arise?

questions.prompt: What term describes the Aa parent, which carries two different alleles at this gene?
hints: The term contrasts with homozygous.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Aa is heterozygous; its two different alleles can separate into gametes.

questions.onCorrect: Heterozygous. Two different alleles, so it can pass on either one.

misconceptions.feedback: Homozygous means both alleles are the same. Aa has two different ones.

questions.prompt: For Aa × Aa, what percentage of offspring is expected to have genotype aa?
hints: Look at all four pairings.
Count the aa boxes.
Convert the fraction of boxes to a percentage.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: One of four equally likely pairings is aa: 1 ÷ 4 = 25%.

questions.onCorrect: 25%. One box in four is aa, and each box is equally likely.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the chance of Aa. aa fills only one box.
That is the chance of the dominant phenotype. The question asks about genotype aa.

questions.prompt: With A completely dominant, which genotypes have the dominant phenotype?
hints: Keep genotype letters separate from the expressed trait.

acceptedIdeas: Two dominant alleles, or one of each
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: One A allele is enough for the dominant phenotype in this model.

choices.label: Two dominant alleles, or one of each

questions.onCorrect: AA and Aa both. One dominant allele is enough to show the dominant trait.

misconceptions.feedback: Two recessive alleles give the recessive trait. Look for the genotypes that hide it.
Every organism has two alleles at the gene, so one of the options must apply.

questions.prompt: Four offspring are produced from Aa × Aa. Which statement is justified?
hints: A probability describes the long-run pattern.

acceptedIdeas: Each has a 25% chance of being aa
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Independent random outcomes do not enforce a fixed family quota.

choices.label: Each has a 25% chance of being aa

questions.onCorrect: Each offspring has the same chance. Four children need not include exactly one aa.

misconceptions.feedback: Each birth is independent. A family can have none, or several.
A quarter of pairings are aa, so each child has a chance of it.

questions.prompt: For Aa × aa, what percentage of offspring is expected to show the recessive phenotype?
hints: The aa parent always passes on a.
The Aa parent passes on a half the time.
Convert that fraction to a percentage.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Two of four equally likely pairings are aa: 2 ÷ 4 = 50%.

questions.onCorrect: 50%. Only aa shows the recessive trait, and half the offspring are aa.

misconceptions.feedback: The Aa parent passes on A half the time, and those offspring show the dominant trait.
That is the chance for Aa × Aa. This cross has an aa parent, which changes the odds.

questions.prompt: In this model, Aa and AA share a phenotype. What term describes A relative to a?
hints: Name how the allele is expressed, not how common it is.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: A is dominant in this genotype-to-phenotype relationship; that does not establish its frequency or fitness effect.

questions.onCorrect: Dominant. It shows whenever it is present, but that says nothing about how common it is.

misconceptions.feedback: The recessive allele is the one that shows only with two copies. A shows with one.
Dominance is about expression. It does not mean the allele is common.

questions.prompt: For Aa × Aa, what percentage of offspring is expected to show the dominant phenotype?
hints: List the four pairings.
Which genotypes show the dominant trait?
Count those boxes out of four.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: AA, Aa and Aa show the dominant trait: 3 ÷ 4 = 75%.

questions.onCorrect: 75%. AA and Aa both show the dominant trait, and together they fill three boxes of four.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the chance of aa only. Count every genotype that shows the dominant trait.
That counts Aa alone. AA shows the dominant trait too.

questions.prompt: Two parents both show the dominant trait, but their child shows the recessive trait. What word describes each parent's genotype?
hints: The child must have received a recessive allele from each parent.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Each parent must carry one recessive allele without showing it, so each is heterozygous.

questions.onCorrect: Heterozygous. Each parent hid a recessive allele and passed it on.

misconceptions.feedback: A parent with two dominant alleles could not pass on a recessive one.

questions.prompt: What is the chance, as a percentage, that both coins land heads?
hints: Write out every combination of the two coins.
There are four equally likely combinations.
How many of those four have two heads?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT. One of the four is HH: 1 ÷ 4 = 25%.

questions.onCorrect: 25%. List the equally likely outcomes and count the ones you want. A cross works the same way.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the chance for one coin. Both coins must land heads.
Each coin could land tails, so both heads is not certain.

questions.prompt: How many boxes does the Punnett square for Aa × Aa have?
hints: Each parent makes two kinds of gamete.
Each box pairs one gamete from each parent.
Multiply the kinds of gamete from the two parents.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each parent makes two kinds of gamete, so there are 2 × 2 = 4 pairings.

questions.onCorrect: 4. Two kinds of gamete from each parent make four equally likely pairings.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the kinds of gamete from one parent. The square pairs gametes from both.
Every pairing of the two parents' gametes gets a box, and that is more than three.

questions.prompt: Why does Aa fill two boxes in the Aa × Aa square?
hints: Think about which parent gives which allele.

acceptedIdeas: A and a can meet in either order, so two boxes give Aa
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The Aa genotype can be made in two ways, so it fills two of the four boxes.

choices.label: Aa is more likely because it is dominant
A and a can meet in either order, so two boxes give Aa

questions.onCorrect: There are two ways to make Aa, so it fills two of the four boxes.

misconceptions.feedback: Dominance affects the trait you see. It does not change how often a genotype forms.
Both boxes are correct. Each shows a different way to make the same genotype.
